# Specification: USB 2.0 Protocol Constants Package

## 1. Scope

This unit provides static definitions for a set of USB 2.0 protocol constants. It defines numeric encodings for:

- USB Packet Identifier (PID) type categories.
- USB Packet Identifier (PID) values.
- Standard USB setup request codes.
- USB descriptor types.

The unit has no runtime state and does not perform packet processing. It only makes the following named constant values available to the rest of the design.

## 2. Packet Identifier Type Categories

A USB PID is a 4-bit value. The low two bits of the PID identify its category. The unit must define the following category codes:

| PID Type | Type Code |
|----------|-----------|
| Special   | 00b |
| Token     | 01b |
| Handshake | 10b |
| Data      | 11b |

## 3. Packet Identifier Values

The unit must define the following USB 2.0 PID values. These values are 4-bit codes.

### Token PIDs

| PID Name | Value |
|----------|-------|
| OUT   | 0001b |
| IN    | 1001b |
| SOF   | 0101b |
| SETUP | 1101b |

### Data PIDs

| PID Name | Value |
|----------|-------|
| DATA0 | 0011b |
| DATA1 | 1011b |
| DATA2 | 0111b |
| MDATA | 1111b |

### Handshake PIDs

| PID Name | Value |
|----------|-------|
| ACK   | 0010b |
| NAK   | 1010b |
| STALL | 1110b |
| NYET  | 0110b |

### Special PIDs

| PID Name | Value |
|----------|-------|
| PRE | 1100b |

For every PID value, the low two bits must match the corresponding PID type category defined in Section 2.

## 4. Standard Setup Request Codes

The unit must define the following standard setup request codes. These are 8-bit unsigned values, shown here in decimal.

| Standard Request | Value |
|------------------|-------|
| GET_STATUS        | 0  |
| CLEAR_FEATURE     | 1  |
| SET_FEATURE       | 3  |
| SET_ADDRESS       | 5  |
| GET_DESCRIPTOR    | 6  |
| SET_DESCRIPTOR    | 7  |
| GET_CONFIGURATION | 8  |
| SET_CONFIGURATION | 9  |
| GET_INTERFACE     | 10 |
| SET_INTERFACE     | 11 |
| SYNCH_FRAME       | 12 |

## 5. Descriptor Type Codes

The unit must define the following USB descriptor type codes. These are 8-bit unsigned values, shown here in decimal.

| Descriptor Type | Value |
|-----------------|-------|
| Device                    | 1 |
| Configuration             | 2 |
| String                    | 3 |
| Interface                 | 4 |
| Endpoint                  | 5 |
| Device Qualifier          | 6 |
| Other Speed Configuration | 7 |
| Interface Power           | 8 |

## 6. Behavioral Requirements

- The constant values must be static and unchanging during operation.
- The unit must not modify, recalculate, or override any constant value at runtime.
- The PID values must match USB 2.0 Table 8-1.
- The setup request codes must match USB 2.0 Table 9-4.
- The descriptor type codes must match USB 2.0 Table 9-5.
- The PID type code for each PID must be derivable from the low two bits of that PID value.
- The unit shall provide exactly the constants listed in this specification; no additional runtime behavior is required.

# USB Full-Speed Receiver Functional Specification

## 1. Overview

This module implements the receive path for a USB 2.0 Full-Speed interface. It samples the USB differential bus, recovers the 12 Mbps bit timing from the received data, decodes NRZI data, removes bit stuffing, detects packet boundaries, extracts PID, token, and data fields, checks PID and CRC correctness, and reports packet validity and error conditions.

All behavior is synchronous to the required 48 MHz clock.

---

## 2. Reset and Initialization

- An asynchronous reset shall clear all receiver state and place the receiver in the idle, no-packet state.
- A link reset input shall have the same effect on packet processing: it shall clear packet boundary state, PID state, CRC state, bit-stuff state, token payload state, and any decoded data or status outputs.

---

## 3. Configuration Behavior

The receiver shall support the following configuration modes:

### 3.1 D+/D- Pin Swap

- When pin swap is enabled, the receiver shall logically swap the D+ and D- inputs.
- The differential data polarity shall be inverted in this mode so that the same J/K/SE0 symbol interpretation is preserved.

### 3.2 Receive Source Selection

The receiver shall support two receive modes:

- **Direct D+/D- mode:** J, K, and SE0 symbols are recovered from the D+ and D- inputs.
- **External differential receiver mode:** J and K symbols are recovered from the differential receiver data input. The D+/D- pair shall still be used to detect the SE0 state.
  - When SE0 is present on D+/D-, the SE0 state shall take precedence over any value from the differential receiver.
  - The differential receiver valid indication shall be required for packet acceptance. When it is deasserted, the current packet shall be invalidated and no new packet shall be considered valid.

### 3.3 EOP Detection Threshold

- The receiver shall detect end-of-packet when the line is in the SE0 state.
- It shall support a configuration that allows EOP to be recognized after a single SE0 bit period. When this mode is not enabled, the receiver shall require two consecutive SE0 bit periods before declaring end-of-packet.

### 3.4 Transmit Disable

- While the transmit enable input is asserted, the receiver shall ignore the incoming USB bus and force the received line state to the idle J state.
- While transmitting, the receiver shall not report start-of-packet, end-of-packet, idle detection, or J detection.

---

## 4. Clock Recovery and Bit Timing

- The receiver shall recover the USB bit clock from transitions on the received line state.
- Each transition between J, K, and SE0 states shall be used to resynchronize the bit timing.
- The receiver shall produce a bit-strobe pulse once per recovered bit period.
- The recovered bit timing shall be aligned so that data is sampled near the center of each bit interval.

---

## 5. Line State Recovery

- The receiver shall recover the USB line states J, K, and SE0.
- J and K are the differential idle and non-idle states.
- SE0 is the single-ended zero state used for end-of-packet.

- The receiver shall tolerate short transition periods during which D+ and D- may not yet have settled to the same state. A transition indication shall not be interpreted as a valid J, K, or SE0 symbol until the line state has stabilized.

---

## 6. Packet Boundary Detection

### 6.1 Start-of-Packet

- When the receiver is idle, not transmitting, and not already inside a packet, a transition from J to K shall be treated as the start-of-packet symbol.
- The receiver shall produce a start-of-packet pulse when this J-to-K transition is detected.
- This pulse marks the beginning of the USB SYNC field.
- The receiver shall recognize a valid USB SYNC pattern before treating the following contents as a valid packet.

### 6.2 End-of-Packet

- The receiver shall produce an end-of-packet indication when the current packet terminates.
- Normal packet termination occurs when SE0 is detected for the configured EOP duration.
- The receiver shall also terminate the current packet early when:
  - a bit-stuff violation is detected, or
  - a PRE PID is recognized.
- In these early-termination cases, the end-of-packet output shall still be generated.

---

## 7. NRZI Decoding and Bit Stuffing

- The receiver shall decode USB non-return-to-zero inverted (NRZI) data from the recovered line states.
- The receiver shall remove bit-stuffed zeros inserted after six consecutive ones on the wire.
- If seven consecutive ones are observed before bit-stuff removal, the receiver shall record a bit-stuff error.
- A packet with a bit-stuff error shall be invalidated and terminated.

---

## 8. PID and Packet Type Handling

- The receiver shall assemble the 8-bit PID field and check that the PID complement matches the PID value.
- The decoded 4-bit PID shall be presented on the PID output.
- The PID determines the packet class:
  - **Token packets** have a token payload and CRC5.
  - **Data packets** have a data phase and CRC16.
  - **Handshake packets** have no payload.
  - **Preamble (PRE)** is recognized as a special packet terminator and is not treated as a normal data, token, or handshake packet.

- If the PID complement check fails, the receiver shall report a PID error at end-of-packet.

---

## 9. Token Packet Decoding

- For token packets, the receiver shall extract the 11-bit token payload that follows the PID.
- For SETUP, IN, and OUT token packets, the payload shall be decoded as:
  - 7-bit device address
  - 4-bit endpoint number
- For SOF token packets, the payload shall be decoded as an 11-bit frame number.
- The decoded address, endpoint, and frame number outputs shall be updated when a token packet is received and shall remain stable until a later token packet updates them.
- The token payload shall be checked with CRC5.

---

## 10. Data Packet Decoding

- For data packets, the receiver shall deserialize the serial bit stream following the PID into 8-bit bytes.
- Each time a byte is assembled, the receiver shall assert a data-put output for one clock period and present the byte on the data output.
- Data output shall be produced only for data PID packets. Token and handshake packets shall not produce data output.
- The data packet payload shall be checked with CRC16.

---

## 11. Packet Validity

A packet shall be considered valid only if all of the following conditions are satisfied:

- The PID complement is valid.
- No bit-stuff error occurred.
- For token packets, the CRC5 check passes.
- For data packets, the CRC16 check passes.
- For handshake packets, no CRC is required, but the PID and bit-stuff conditions still apply.

The packet-valid output shall be asserted when the most recently received packet meets these conditions. It shall be deasserted for any packet that fails any applicable check.

---

## 12. Error Reporting

The receiver shall provide the following error indications:

| Error Condition | Behavior |
|---|---|
| PID complement mismatch | PID error indication at end-of-packet |
| CRC5 or CRC16 mismatch | CRC error indication at end-of-packet |
| Bit-stuff violation | Bit-stuff error indication at end-of-packet |

- CRC error shall only be reported for token and data packets, not for handshake packets.
- Any packet with a detected error shall not be reported as valid.

---

## 13. Status Outputs

The receiver shall provide the following line-status outputs:

- **Idle detection:** shall be asserted when the recovered line state is J and the transmitter is disabled.
- **J detection:** shall be asserted when the most recently recovered line symbol is J, the transmitter is disabled, and the differential receiver input is valid.

These outputs are intended to indicate the actual received line condition after clock recovery and are not asserted during transmit.
